title: The whole app runs on one MacBook at home, and it is on battery right now
evidence: Live GET https://relay.anjiawenda.com/api/health 2026-11-21 15:58Z: 'mac_on_battery ... The Mac is running on battery (80% left). Plug it in: when the battery runs out, Pexi goes down.' plus two 'mac_job_stale' problems (disk, integrity); watch ok:false. Commit 4786ec6: 'it ran flat 2026-11-18, Pexi down 2 hours'. RULINGS.md:722-733 backend hosted on his own Mac. Apple's submit checklist: 'Enable backend services so that they're live and accessible during review.' A home power or internet cut, a macOS restart or a flat battery means every shopper gets no answer and App Review sees a broken app.
fix: Today: plug in, add a UPS, and have the health watch page someone (not just log) on battery or stale jobs. Before a public push: run the same server on a small cloud VM (or a second machine) behind the same tunnel name as failover.
fix_cost: UPS about $150 and 1 hour; cloud VM about $20-40 a month and 1-2 days

title: No purchase has ever been completed, but the free limit is already on
evidence: NOW.md:100 'Paywall purchase (launch gaps 7) still not run.' NOW.md:103 'The free limit is ON live (2026-11-18 15:10Z, /api/quota answers limit: 10)'. NOW.md:58-59 build 8/9 'none of it seen on a phone'. app/src/scan-quota.ts entitlementStartupWarning: if REVENUECAT_SECRET_KEY is unset 'nobody is Pexi Plus on this server, paying subscribers included' (only a startup log line; /api/health does not report the mode). docs/store/listing.md:172: an empty RevenueCat iOS key in the build 'shows no plans'. Either gap means a shopper pays and is still refused at 10.
fix: Sandbox-buy on build 10, then confirm the server returns plus:true for that phone; add entitlement mode (revenuecat vs client_trusted) to /api/health so it is visible; confirm both products are attached to the 1.0 version in App Store Connect.

title: A subscription only works on the phone that bought it; Restore on a second phone likely moves it away from the first
evidence: app/public/js/purchases.js:82 configures RevenueCat with appUserID: getDeviceId().id (a random id per phone); app/src/scan-quota.ts isPlus asks RevenueCat about that one device id. Apple guideline 3.1.2(a): the subscription must 'be available across all of the user's devices'. With custom app user ids, RevenueCat's restore by default transfers the purchase to the new id (ASSUMED from RevenueCat's documented default, project setting not read), so a two-phone household ping-pongs Plus and the server refuses one phone.
fix: Check the RevenueCat project's restore behaviour; let a second phone share the purchase (send the RevenueCat original app user id the phone reports and have the server check that id), and test with two phones on one Apple ID.

title: App Store Connect said 'unlimited scans' and 148 countries; the product is 100 a week and Canada only
evidence: docs/launch-gaps-2026-11-06.md:184-187 (checked in App Store Connect 11-07): 'Description and review notes say unlimited scans; subscriptions say 100 a week' and 'Availability is 148 countries; ruling is Canada only' (docs/decisions.md:3088). Result of the fix was 'to be recorded here' and is not. A US or UK shopper gets Canadian-only prices and leaves one star; 'unlimited' on a 100-a-week plan is a metadata accuracy rejection or refund cause.
fix: Open App Store Connect: set availability to Canada only, paste the text from docs/store/listing.md, re-read it.

title: Claude price ranges stop for everyone after 1,000 asks a month
evidence: identify/src/range-ask.ts:208 DEFAULT_MONTHLY_CAP = 1000; settings/src/index.ts:81 SHIN_RANGE_ASK_MONTHLY_CAP default 1000 asks per UTC month, one pool for all users. Model is claude-haiku-4-5 (range-ask.ts:213), so 1,000 asks cost a few dollars. NOW.md:66 'Only 27% of 176 real scans had a shop price', so most unpriced scans want a range. With thousands of users the pool is gone in days and every unpriced item falls to broad guesses until the 1st. The live value of the setting is unknown (health shows reached:false today).
fix: Set SHIN_RANGE_ASK_MONTHLY_CAP to a number sized to users (e.g. 30,000) and alarm on dollars spent, not asks; the per-device and per-network limits already stop one abuser.
fix_cost: 10 minutes; about $30-60 a month at 30,000 asks (assumed token sizes)

title: Shoppers on a store's Wi-Fi get told they used all 10 free scans on their first scan
evidence: app/src/rate-limit.ts:173 SHIN_FREE_SCANS_PER_IP_DAY default 150 free barcode scans per address per day; app/server.ts:3201-3205 when that address is over, a first-time shopper gets 402 with 'limit: free, used: free' so the paywall reads '10 of 10 used' (paywall-strings.js:17). Claude asks are also capped at 250 a day per /24 network (server.ts:1665). A grocery store's guest Wi-Fi or a carrier NAT puts many shoppers behind one address. That a store Wi-Fi reaches 150 a day is ASSUMED.
fix: Raise the per-address ceiling (e.g. 2,000) and when the address, not the phone, is over, show a 'busy, try again shortly' message instead of a false '10 of 10 used'.

title: Paying subscribers can be refused as free users at busy times
evidence: app/server.ts:3201 freeScanAddressRefusal calls isPlus on every barcode scan; app/src/scan-quota.ts:57 one global limit of 120 RevenueCat lookups a minute, entitlement cached only 10 minutes (ENTITLEMENT_CACHE_MS). Over the limit isPlus returns the stale cached answer or a 24-hour 'recently Plus' grace, so a subscriber who just bought (cached false) or has not opened the app for a day is answered as free and sees the paywall. A cache miss also waits up to 3 s on RevenueCat before the scan answers.
fix: Cache a true entitlement until RevenueCat's expires_date, add the RevenueCat webhook to update it, and only ask RevenueCat when a free phone reaches its limit.

title: One script can saturate the home upload by downloading the 44 MB product pack
evidence: curl https://relay.anjiawenda.com/api/pack?scope=canada without compression: 44,143,820 bytes in 3.65 s (12 MB/s); header 'cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC' so Cloudflare does not cache it although it is 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable'. /api/pack has no route limit (server.ts:4449-4453); the address limit is 6,000 requests per 10 minutes (rate-limit.ts:149). Also every pack version change makes every installed phone download it again (app/public/js/pack.js:259-294), about 6.8 MB each from the Mac.
fix: Add a Cloudflare cache rule for /api/pack* (versioned URL), or host the pack on Cloudflare R2 or a GitHub release; refuse uncompressed pack requests.

title: 'Early access' banner invites a beta rejection
evidence: app/public/js/ui-strings.js:272-273 ea_badge 'Early access', ea_title 'Pexi is in early access', shown on the first camera visit (screen-tags.js:179). Apple guideline 2.2: 'Demos, betas, and trial versions of your app don't belong on the App Store - use TestFlight instead.' Whether a reviewer flags this wording is ASSUMED.
fix: Keep the message, drop the words 'early access' (say what it knows best, e.g. everyday groceries).

title: Most scans have no real shop price, so most first answers are estimates
evidence: NOW.md:66 'Only 27% of 176 real scans had a shop price.' docs/store/listing.md:40 'it may show a typical price range that an AI model estimated. Estimates can be wrong.' A new user's first few scans decide whether they keep the app; a confident 'Bad price' on an estimate, or 'no price here yet', at scale shows up as one-star reviews and no conversions.
fix: Measure the top scanned barcodes from the beta and fill prices for those first; make sure every estimate answer looks visibly different from a shop-price answer.

title: Free users lose almost nothing at the limit, so few will pay
evidence: RULINGS.md:469-476 'typed searches are free and uncounted'; the paywall itself says 'Typing a name still works and everything you saved is still here.' (app/public/js/paywall-strings.js:18). The only thing Plus adds is barcode scans 11 to 100 a week.
fix: Decide what Plus uniquely gives (e.g. Claude ranges, watch-list alerts, store comparison) or count typed answers too; A/B the paywall line.

title: Small Business Program enrolment not recorded (15% vs 30% Apple fee)
evidence: docs/decisions.md:2948 revenue figures assume 'US$2.44 at 15% (Small Business Program) or US$2.01 at 30%'. No record in the repo of enrolling. Without it Apple keeps 30% of first-year subscription revenue.
fix: Enrol in the App Store Small Business Program in the developer account before launch.

title: The whole API is open to any script, and the health page shows the server's weak moments
evidence: Live: /api/search?q=milk with no invite header answered 200 with catalogue rows; /api/quota answered 403 only for the device proof, so the invite gate is off. Device ids cost nothing to make. /api/health (no auth) shows battery %, stale jobs, disk free, Claude cap state and backup times.
fix: Trim /api/health to ok and uptime for the public, move the rest behind the admin token; accept the open API but keep the per-address limits.

title: French users get English Terms and Privacy on the subscribe screen
evidence: app/public/js/screens/paywall.js:302-303 and :358-359, screens/you.js:456,460 use LEGAL_URLS.terms/privacy (English); screens/agree.js:78-79 uses legalUrl(kind, lang), and plus-config.js:51 notes 'Quebec requires consumer contracts in French'. French pages are live (terms-fr.html, privacy-fr.html answered 200).
fix: Use legalUrl(kind, lang) in paywall.js and you.js.

title: No French App Store listing
evidence: docs/store/listing.md has English text only; the app ships French strings (ui-strings.js:867 onward). Quebec shoppers see an English store page; Quebec's language law covers commercial advertising (ASSUMED to reach a store page).
fix: Add a French (Canada) localization of the listing from the existing French strings.

title: Off-site backup destination may never have been chosen
evidence: mac/14-offsite-backup.sh:14 the destination (b2 or s3) 'Jamin picks it'. Local backups exist (/api/health newestBackupAt 2026-11-21T09:15Z) but on the same laptop. A stolen, dropped or dead MacBook loses scan history, shopper prices and corrections. Whether the off-site job is configured on the Mac was not checked.
fix: Pick a bucket (Backblaze B2 is pennies a month), run --init, then the restore test.

title: Deletion requests are done by hand from a Gmail address
evidence: docs/store/privacy.html: 'Open the You screen and tap Delete my data, which prepares an email to useshinapp@gmail... Deletion is done by hand.' The address still carries the old project name (listing.md:78,180). At tens of thousands of users each request is manual work with a 30-day legal clock, and an email does not prove the sender owns the device id.
fix: An in-app Delete my data button that calls a server route proven by the device key and deletes at once; a Pexi-named support address.

title: Store lookups depend on a free public map server with a 10,000-a-day limit
evidence: app/src/stores.ts:302 'https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter', in-memory cache of 500 cells (stores.ts:340). Overpass usage policy: 'No more than 10,000 queries per day and download no more than 1 GB data per day.' Location is off by default, so volume is ASSUMED.
fix: Persist the cell cache to disk with a larger ceiling and set SHIN_OVERPASS to a paid or self-hosted instance once location users pass a few thousand.

title: iPhone build allows landscape, which the screens do not handle
evidence: native/ios/App/App/Info.plist UISupportedInterfaceOrientations lists LandscapeLeft and LandscapeRight for iPhone; a grep for 'orientation' in app/public/css and js finds nothing. A rotated camera screen is what a reviewer may see.
fix: Keep only UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait for iPhone.

title: Nothing stops the database disk from filling
evidence: app/src/disk-guard.ts (2 GB floor) is used only for the shutter log (server.ts:2574); scans, events and the access log write without a check. Health shows 46.6 GB free today. Usage events are kept 12 months (privacy.html). Growth at thousands of users is ASSUMED; a full disk makes every write, and likely every scan, fail.
fix: Add free disk to the health watch with a page at 10 GB, and drop event writes (not scans) below the floor.

title: A phone whose stored secret is lost is locked out for good
evidence: app/src/device-key.ts bindDevice is INSERT OR IGNORE and ownsDevice refuses a wrong key with no re-bind path; app/public/js/device.js reconcile writes id and secret to the Keychain separately. If the id survives without its secret, every request answers 'That request is about a device it cannot prove it is.' (seen live on /api/quota), including for a subscriber. How often this happens is ASSUMED rare.
fix: On that refusal the phone makes a fresh id and secret and calls RevenueCat logIn so Plus follows.
